segments.t: Configure custom AI skills that enhance AI interactions. This tab lets you manage a library of markdown-based skills that are automatically or manually included in AI requests. Open via KTPH001AI → AI Manager → AI SkillsKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.

The skill library used to be a tab in KTPH000Configuration → Global SettingsKTPH001. It now lives in the KTPH002AI ManagerKTPH003, next to profiles, local models and knowledge stores. The stored data and the settings file are unchanged.
Filters the list by name, description or tags
Writes the library to the global settings file

A count line below the list summarizes the whole library — KTPH000TotalKTPH001, KTPH002ActiveKTPH003 (enabled and not hidden), and KTPH004Inactive/hiddenKTPH005 — regardless of the current search or hidden filter.
When you select or create a skill, the right panel shows per-skill fields. Each skill is persisted individually in the skill list.
AI Chat/Functions, AI Agent, Both, Connection

korTTY ships 39 built-in best-practice skills covering shells (Bash, KornShell, Zsh, Csh, POSIX sh, PowerShell), programming languages (Python, C, C++, Java, C#, JavaScript, Visual Basic, SQL, R, Rust, Go, PHP, Swift, Assembly, Macro Assembler, Ruby, Perl, Lua, Groovy, TypeScript, Kotlin, Dart), markup and data formats (HTML, XML, YAML, JSON) and automation/observability tools (Puppet, Ansible, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Jenkins Declarative and Scripted Pipelines, Filebeat, Logstash). Each skill carries professional guidance on code commenting, robustness, common pitfalls to avoid, and language-specific security practices. They are added to the library on first start and appear with a KTPH000Built-inKTPH001 badge.
Built-in skills behave like your own skills — they can be edited, deactivated and assigned to connections — with these differences:

KTPH000They cannot be deleted, only hidden.KTPH001 KTPH002HideKTPH003 removes a built-in from the list and from all skill pickers, and a hidden built-in is no longer sent with any AI request — even on connections it was previously assigned to. KTPH004Show hidden built-in skillsKTPH005 reveals hidden entries, marked with a KTPH006HiddenKTPH007 badge, so they can be brought back with KTPH008UnhideKTPH009.

KTPH000Unmodified built-ins update automatically.KTPH001 When a new korTTY release ships improved skill content, unchanged built-ins are replaced silently at startup (your Active/hidden choices are kept).

KTPH000Modified built-ins are never touched.KTPH001 Once you edit a built-in it shows a KTPH002Built-in (modified)KTPH003 badge and stops auto-updating. KTPH004Reset to shipped versionKTPH005 discards your changes and restores the delivered version your edits were based on. If a newer delivered version exists, the entry shows 🔄 KTPH006Update availableKTPH007 and KTPH008Update to latest shipped versionKTPH009 adopts it.

KTPH001Your own skills always take precedence.KTPH002 When one of your enabled skills carries a tag matching a built-in's topic (for example a personal skill tagged KTPH000), the built-in is suppressed: it shows KTPH003Overridden by user skillKTPH004, is grayed out, and is no longer sent with any AI request. Deleting or deactivating your skill immediately reactivates the built-in.
Deactivated, hidden and overridden entries are rendered grayed out; this works in every application design theme.

Without auto-detection every enabled skill is sent with every AI request, which would inflate prompts massively with 39 built-in skills. Turning KTPH000Automatically send only matching skillsKTPH001 off therefore asks for confirmation and then deactivates all built-in skills; re-enable the ones you need individually. Built-ins delivered by later releases also arrive deactivated while auto-detection is off.

When KTPH000Automatically send only matching skillsKTPH001 is enabled, korTTY scores each skill against the current request across four fields — tags, name, description, and the headings in the skill's Markdown — and includes at most the KTPH002twoKTPH003 highest-scoring skills that clear the relevance threshold (ties broken by catalog order). Explicitly pinned and connection-assigned skills are added on top and do not consume that limit. When the local scores are inconclusive (zero or one skill matched, or exactly two matched with nearly equal scores), korTTY additionally asks the model to classify the request and prefers that answer — likewise capped at two skills — falling back to the local result if the call fails. When disabled, all applicable skills are sent without scoring — a skill is still skipped when it is inactive, has empty content, or does not match the current target.
KTPH000AI Chat/FunctionsKTPH001: Skills available in AI Chat and function call contexts
KTPH000AI AgentKTPH001: Skills used by the terminal AI agent
KTPH000BothKTPH001: Available to both AI Chat and AI Agent contexts
KTPH000ConnectionKTPH001: Available to both AI Chat and AI Agent, but only on the connections the skill is assigned to. Such skills are always sent on those connections and bypass auto-detection.

Skills are stored as XML elements within the global settings file. Use KTPH000ImportKTPH001 to load skills from markdown files and KTPH002ExportKTPH003 to save selected skills as markdown files. KTPH004DeleteKTPH005 applies to your own skills only; built-in skills are hidden instead (see above). Reset, update, hide and unhide are available from the list's context menu and from the banner above the editor when a built-in skill is selected. The skill list can be sorted alphabetically by name or by status (enabled first). KTPH006SaveKTPH007 persists the library immediately and confirms next to the button; pending edits are also written when the AI Manager window is closed. Importing a markdown file always creates an independent user skill — even a file exported from a built-in skill.

This tab manages the global library. Which of these enabled skills apply to a given action is chosen elsewhere: the snippet editor's KTPH000AI skillsKTPH001 picker pins your selection to every snippet AI action, and the KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 window shows the included skills as chips — labelled KTPH004(auto-selected)KTPH005 or KTPH006(manual)KTPH007 — with a searchable picker whose changes take effect on the next re-run. Within snippet AI actions the picker replaces auto-detection: only the ticked skills plus connection-assigned skills are sent, and clearing the picker sends no library skills at all. The snippet KTPH008CorrectKTPH009 and KTPH010TranslateKTPH011 selection actions and the fixed KTPH012DiagramKTPH013 request never include library skills, regardless of target or pinning. See KTPH014Snippets → AI skillsKTPH015.
